english: You're quite social, aren't you? How charming.
french: Tu aimes avoir de la compagnie, n'est-ce pas ? C'est charmant.
russian: Ты общительное создание, как я погляжу. Очаровательно.
bulgarian: You're quite social, aren't you? How charming.

english: Whether it be whimsy or vanity... I cannot help but find it flattering.
french: Que ce soit par fantaisie ou par vanité... je ne puis m'empêcher de trouver cela flatteur.
russian: Возможно, во мне говорит тщеславие... но это не может не льстить.
bulgarian: Whether it be whimsy or vanity... I cannot help but find it flattering.

english: The stone font in the bath looks to be a statue of... me.
french: La fontaine de pierre, dans les bains, semble être une statue de... moi.
russian: Фонтанная статуя в купальне, по-видимому, изображает... меня.
bulgarian: The stone font in the bath looks to be a statue of... me.

english: The waters of this bathhouse are quite special...
french: L'eau de ces bains est très particulière...
russian: В этой купальне крайне необычная вода...
bulgarian: The waters of this bathhouse are quite special...

english: Most scents are simple to the keen nose of a dragon, but the steamy bouquet here is quite complex.
french: La plupart des odeurs sont très simples, pour l'odorat aiguisé d'un dragon, mais les vapeurs parfumées de ce lieu sont fort complexes.
russian: Для чуткого нюха дракона большинство запахов звучат незатейливо. Но здешний букет ароматов весьма изысканный.
bulgarian: Most scents are simple to the keen nose of a dragon, but the steamy bouquet here is quite complex.

english: The mistress of this bathhouse is very skilled at developing bath oils.
french: La maîtresse de cette maison de bains a un réel talent pour créer des huiles de bain.
russian: Хозяйка купальни — настоящая мастерица в маслах для ванн.
bulgarian: The mistress of this bathhouse is very skilled at developing bath oils.

english: It fits into this hot springs bath, for one.
french: Notamment celui de pouvoir entrer dans ce bain de sources chaudes.
russian: Например, оно хорошо помещается в эту горячую ванну.
bulgarian: It fits into this hot springs bath, for one.

english: This mortal form has its advantages...
french: Cette forme mortelle a certains avantages...
russian: У смертного обличья есть свои преимущества...
bulgarian: This mortal form has its advantages...

english: As with all things, the natural world is constantly evolving.
french: Comme toute chose, le monde naturel est en perpétuelle évolution.
russian: Природа непрерывно изменяется, как и всё в этом мире.
bulgarian: As with all things, the natural world is constantly evolving.

english: I find this impermanence quite beautiful.
french: Je trouve cette fugacité magnifique.
russian: И в этом непостоянстве я вижу красоту.
bulgarian: I find this impermanence quite beautiful.

english: The shoreline of Mistria has undergone many changes since the first time I first laid eyes upon it...
french: Le trait de côte de Mistria a connu bien des transformations depuis la première fois où j'ai posé les yeux dessus...
russian: Очертания мистрийского берега неоднократно менялись с той поры, когда я его впервые увидел...
bulgarian: The shoreline of Mistria has undergone many changes since the first time I first laid eyes upon it...

english: Though if one is not careful, one risks being lulled to sleep.
french: Si l'on n'y prend garde, il peut nous bercer jusqu'au sommeil.
russian: Он так убаюкивает, что под него можно незаметно заснуть.
bulgarian: Though if one is not careful, one risks being lulled to sleep.

english: The rhythm of the ocean is like music, and quite meditative...
french: Le rythme de l'océan est semblable à une musique et invite à la méditation...
russian: Ритм океана подобен музыке. Такой медитативный...
bulgarian: The rhythm of the ocean is like music, and quite meditative...

english: I began to wonder if it would live up to my memories.
french: J'avais commencé à me demander s'il serait à la hauteur de mes souvenirs.
russian: Я стал переживать, действительно ли он так хорош, как я его помню.
bulgarian: I began to wonder if it would live up to my memories.

english: I was wrong to worry. It is more beautiful than I remember.
french: J'avais tort de m'inquiéter. Il est plus beau encore que dans ma mémoire.
russian: Но я волновался напрасно. Океан красивее всех моих ожиданий.
bulgarian: I was wrong to worry. It is more beautiful than I remember.

english: Whilst convalescing in the Deep Woods, my mind wandered often to thoughts of the ocean.
french: Pendant ma convalescence à Boissombre, mon esprit vagabondait souvent en pensant à l'océan.
russian: Когда я выздоравливал в Глубокой чаще, мой разум часто посещали мысли об океане.
bulgarian: Whilst convalescing in the Deep Woods, my mind wandered often to thoughts of the ocean.

english: Yes... the Beach is full of pleasant dichotomies.
french: Oui... la plage est si pleine d'agréables dichotomies.
russian: Да уж... На пляже много занимательных контрастов.
bulgarian: Yes... the Beach is full of pleasant dichotomies.

english: I enjoy watching the cool waters of the ocean meet the hot sand of the shore.
french: J'aime regarder les eaux froides de l'océan venir à la rencontre du sable chaud de la rive.
russian: Я люблю смотреть, как холодные океанские воды сталкиваются с горячим песком на берегу.
bulgarian: I enjoy watching the cool waters of the ocean meet the hot sand of the shore.

english: The long walk to the Beach is a small thing compared to the promise of its warm sands.
french: La longue marche jusqu'à la plage est peu de chose comparée à la promesse de son sable chaud.
russian: Долгий путь к пляжу — это ничтожная плата за его тёплый песок.
bulgarian: The long walk to the Beach is a small thing compared to the promise of its warm sands.

english: I find that I thrive in the summer heat.
french: Je trouve que tout me convient avec la chaleur de l'été.
russian: Я обнаружил, что отлично себя чувствую в летнюю жару.
bulgarian: I find that I thrive in the summer heat.

english: I am finding it quite enjoyable.
french: Je trouve cela très plaisant.
russian: Это доставляет мне удовольствие.
bulgarian: I am finding it quite enjoyable.

english: In this form, my mouth is much smaller. I am able to take more delicate bites, and savor a meal a little at a time.
french: Sous cette forme, ma bouche est bien plus petite. Je peux prendre des bouchées délicates et savourer un repas petit à petit.
russian: В этом обличии мои уста намного меньше. Я могу вкушать еду медленно, лучше наслаждаться её вкусом.
bulgarian: In this form, my mouth is much smaller. I am able to take more delicate bites, and savor a meal a little at a time.

english: Which is to say, today I learned that char does not taste quite as good in this form.
french: Pour le dire autrement, j'ai découvert aujourd'hui que sous ma forme actuelle, le goût de l'omble n'est pas aussi plaisant.
russian: Например, сегодня я узнал, что гарь не так вкусна для этого обличия.
bulgarian: Which is to say, today I learned that char does not taste quite as good in this form.

english: Of all the challenges I face today, cooking may be the greatest. Every day brings a humbling new lesson.
french: La cuisine est sûrement le plus grand de tous les défis que je dois désormais relever. Chaque jour est l'occasion d'une nouvelle leçon d'humilité.
russian: Из всех испытаний, что стоят передо мной на сегодняшний день, самое сложное — готовка. Каждый день преподносит мне новый урок скромности.
bulgarian: Of all the challenges I face today, cooking may be the greatest. Every day brings a humbling new lesson.

english: Did I always do this? It is difficult to remember.
french: Ai-je toujours fait cela ? Il m'est difficile de m'en souvenir.
russian: Делал ли я это раньше? Тяжело вспомнить.
bulgarian: Did I always do this? It is difficult to remember.

english: I give thanks every time I enjoy the bounty of nature.
french: Je remercie la nature chaque fois que je profite de ses bienfaits.
russian: Я благодарю природу за каждый её дар.
bulgarian: I give thanks every time I enjoy the bounty of nature.

english: I have always made a point to do so.
french: J'en ai toujours fait un point d'honneur.
russian: И я знаю, что делал так всегда.
bulgarian: I have always made a point to do so.

english: I like to give thanks when I enjoy the bounty of nature.
french: J'aime remercier la nature chaque fois que je profite de ses bienfaits.
russian: Мне нравится благодарить природу за каждый её дар.
bulgarian: I like to give thanks when I enjoy the bounty of nature.

english: Is that not funny?
french: N'est-ce pas amusant ?
russian: Разве это не потешно?
bulgarian: Is that not funny?

english: Ah, so it is not. I understand.
french: Ah, ça ne l'est pas. Je comprends.
russian: Ах. Видимо, нет. Я понял.
bulgarian: Ah, so it is not. I understand.

english: The berries in these woods are sometimes sweet, sometimes tart.
french: Les baies que l'on trouve dans ces bois sont parfois sucrées, parfois acides.
russian: Найденные в лесу ягоды на вкус иногда сладкие, а временами кислые.
bulgarian: The berries in these woods are sometimes sweet, sometimes tart.

english: I have been grinding everything I find in my mortar and pestle, and sampling the results.
french: Je mouds tout ce que je trouve grâce à mon pilon et à mon mortier et je goûte le résultat.
russian: Я перетираю всё, что нахожу, в ступке — и пробую результат.
bulgarian: I have been grinding everything I find in my mortar and pestle, and sampling the results.

english: No success yet, but the good news is that my spice cabinet is filling up.
french: En vain, pour l'instant, mais la bonne nouvelle, c'est que mon meuble à épices se remplit à vue d'œil.
russian: Пока безуспешно, но радостно видеть, как заполняется полка с приправами.
bulgarian: No success yet, but the good news is that my spice cabinet is filling up.

english: They say taste can jog the memory, and the tongue of a dragon is particularly keen.
french: On dit qu'un goût peut réactiver un souvenir, et les dragons ont la langue particulièrement sensible.
russian: Говорят, вкусы могут навевать воспоминания. А язык дракона особенно к ним чувствителен.
bulgarian: They say taste can jog the memory, and the tongue of a dragon is particularly keen.

english: I have been grinding everything I find in my mortar and pestle, and sampling the results.
french: Je mouds tout ce que je trouve grâce à mon pilon et à mon mortier et je goûte le résultat.
russian: Я перетираю всё, что нахожу, в ступке — и пробую результат.
bulgarian: I have been grinding everything I find in my mortar and pestle, and sampling the results.

english: I have found that certain tastes seem to jog old memories that were previously unavailable to me.
french: J'ai réalisé que certaines saveurs semblent réactiver d'anciens souvenirs restés jusqu'alors inaccessibles.
russian: Я обнаружил, что некоторые вкусы навевают воспоминания, ранее мне недоступные.
bulgarian: I have found that certain tastes seem to jog old memories that were previously unavailable to me.

english: The tongue of a dragon is particularly keen...
french: Les dragons ont la langue particulièrement sensible...
russian: Язык дракона особенно чувствителен ко вкусам...
bulgarian: The tongue of a dragon is particularly keen...

english: The passage of time brings new cultures, and new cultures bring new food.
french: Au fil du temps, de nouvelles cultures apparaissent et avec elles, une nourriture différente.
russian: С течением времени появляются новые культуры, а вместе с ними — новая еда.
bulgarian: The passage of time brings new cultures, and new cultures bring new food.

english: I am mostly eating simple fare while I acclimate to this form... but I am curious how cuisine has changed while I slept.
french: Tant que je m'habitue encore à cette nouvelle forme, je consomme des aliments simples... Mais je suis curieux de savoir comment la cuisine a évolué pendant mon sommeil.
russian: Сейчас я питаюсь простой едой, привыкая к этой форме... но любопытно, как изменилась кухня за время моего сна.
bulgarian: I am mostly eating simple fare while I acclimate to this form... but I am curious how cuisine has changed while I slept.

english: Fire comes easily to a dragon, so I found it to be a humbling experience.
french: Il est si facile pour un dragon d'avoir du feu... Cette expérience est une leçon d'humilité.
russian: Для дракона огонь — дело простое, потому я почувствовал себя... смиренно.
bulgarian: Fire comes easily to a dragon, so I found it to be a humbling experience.

english: I was preparing to cook, but could not light the fire pit without a struggle.
french: Je m'apprêtais à cuisiner, mais j'ai lutté pour réussir à allumer le foyer.
russian: Я собирался готовить, но с трудом зажёг очаг.
bulgarian: I was preparing to cook, but could not light the fire pit without a struggle.

english: These days, however, I find myself wishing to sample the cooking methods that the modern world offers.
french: Désormais, j'éprouve l'envie d'essayer les méthodes de cuisson qu'offre le monde moderne.
russian: Теперь же я ловлю себя на желании попробовать современные способы приготовления.
bulgarian: These days, however, I find myself wishing to sample the cooking methods that the modern world offers.

english: I recall the thrill of eating freshly caught fish, with no desire to prepare it.
french: Je me souviens du frisson que j'éprouvais en mangeant un poisson fraîchement attrapé, sans avoir nul désir de le préparer.
russian: Я помню, как увлекательно было поедать свежевыловленную рыбу — без всякой готовки.
bulgarian: I recall the thrill of eating freshly caught fish, with no desire to prepare it.

english: If that were the case, I would not have so many troubles.
french: Si c'était le cas, je n'aurais pas tant de difficultés.
russian: Если бы это было так, у меня не возникло бы столько проблем.
bulgarian: If that were the case, I would not have so many troubles.

english: Alas, it is a shame that cooking is not instinctual.
french: Hélas, quel dommage que savoir cuisiner ne soit pas inné !
russian: Увы, жаль, что готовка не заложена в инстинктах.
bulgarian: Alas, it is a shame that cooking is not instinctual.

english: It has taken some adjustment to get used to the... washing of dishes.
french: Il m'a fallu un temps d'adaptation pour m'habituer à... faire la vaisselle.
russian: В этой форме мне пришлось привыкать к... мытью посуды.
bulgarian: It has taken some adjustment to get used to the... washing of dishes.

english: A meal to a dragon is simply food and flame.
french: Pour un dragon, un repas c'est de la nourriture et du feu.
russian: Дракону хватает лишь своего пламени и сырых продуктов, чтобы приступить к трапезе.
bulgarian: A meal to a dragon is simply food and flame.

english: It is my hope that this practice will stir some of the memories I have lost.
french: J'ai l'espoir que cette pratique réveille certains de mes souvenirs perdus.
russian: Надеюсь, эта практика поможет пробудить утраченные воспоминания.
bulgarian: It is my hope that this practice will stir some of the memories I have lost.

english: I enjoy meditating on the flame in my hearth.
french: J'aime méditer en contemplant la flamme de l'âtre.
russian: Мне нравится медитировать, глядя на пламя в очаге.
bulgarian: I enjoy meditating on the flame in my hearth.

english: Perhaps another foraging excursion is in order...
french: Peut-être qu'une nouvelle expédition de récolte s'impose...
russian: Возможно, стоит снова отправиться на поиски съестного...
bulgarian: Perhaps another foraging excursion is in order...

english: Welcome, [Ari]. I am pleased to have you as a guest, though I regret that I cannot offer you much in the way of sustenance.
french: Bienvenue, [Ari]. Je suis ravi de te recevoir, bien que je regrette de n'avoir pas grand-chose à t'offrir pour te sustenter.
russian: Добро пожаловать, [Ari]. Рад видеть тебя у себя в гостях, хоть и сожалею, что не могу предложить угощение.
bulgarian: Welcome, [Ari]. I am pleased to have you as a guest, though I regret that I cannot offer you much in the way of sustenance.

english: In the past, I could rely entirely on my teeth and talons for such work.
french: Par le passé, je pouvais compter sur mes crocs et mes griffes pour ce type de tâche.
russian: Раньше для всех целей мне хватало клыков и когтей.
bulgarian: In the past, I could rely entirely on my teeth and talons for such work.

english: I have never had need of kitchenware such as a knife or cutting board before.
french: Je n'avais autrefois jamais besoin d'ustensiles de cuisine tels qu'un couteau ou une planche à découper.
russian: Я никогда не испытывал необходимости в кухонной утвари вроде ножей или доски для резки.
bulgarian: I have never had need of kitchenware such as a knife or cutting board before.

english: For some reason, my attempts at cake simply will not rise.
french: J'ignore pourquoi, mais mes gâteaux ne lèvent pas.
russian: По неясной мне причине мои пироги не поднимаются.
bulgarian: For some reason, my attempts at cake simply will not rise.

english: [Ari], ah... I was wondering if you could give me some cooking tips.
french: [Ari], euh... Je me demandais si tu pourrais me donner quelques conseils pour cuisiner.
russian: [Ari], ах... Я хотел спросить, сможешь ли ты дать мне несколько советов по готовке.
bulgarian: [Ari], ah... I was wondering if you could give me some cooking tips.

english: Perhaps in the far future...
french: Peut-être que dans un avenir lointain...
russian: Возможно, в делёком будущем...
bulgarian: Perhaps in the far future...

english: I may even be able to write a cookbook!
french: Je serai même capable d'écrire un livre de recettes !
russian: Я смогу написать кулинарную книгу!
bulgarian: I may even be able to write a cookbook!

english: The dishes I am experimenting with are not yet fit to share with company, but I am improving.
french: Les plats que je m'entraîne à préparer ne sont pas encore dignes d'être partagés avec d'autres personnes, mais je progresse.
russian: Блюда, над которыми я экспериментирую, пока не подходят, чтобы разделить их с компанией. Но я делаю успехи.
bulgarian: The dishes I am experimenting with are not yet fit to share with company, but I am improving.

english: I would offer you a bite of the dish I made, but truly... it is my burden to shoulder.
french: J'aimerais te proposer une part de ce que j'ai cuisiné, mais en vérité... C'est à moi d'assumer ce fardeau.
russian: Я бы предложил тебе вкусить блюдо, которое я изготовил, но... это испытание лучше пройти мне самому.
bulgarian: I would offer you a bite of the dish I made, but truly... it is my burden to shoulder.

english: Today I learned that there is such a thing as too much salt.
french: Aujourd'hui, j'ai compris qu'il était possible de trop saler un plat.
russian: Сегодня мне стало известно, что соли может быть слишком много.
bulgarian: Today I learned that there is such a thing as too much salt.

english: To be so accomplished at such a young age is impressive.
french: Il est impressionnant de voir un tel talent chez une personne aussi jeune.
russian: Такие достижения в столь юном возрасте по-настоящему восхищают.
bulgarian: To be so accomplished at such a young age is impressive.

english: The cook at the Inn... Reina. I have a new appreciation for her skill with a pot and pan.
french: Reina, la cuisinière de l'auberge... Je mesure mieux à présent combien elle est douée aux fourneaux.
russian: Рейна, трактирская повариха... Теперь мне представилась возможность должным образом оценить её навыки.
bulgarian: The cook at the Inn... Reina. I have a new appreciation for her skill with a pot and pan.

english: It seems some wild plants are not "edible" in my current form.
french: Apparemment, certaines plantes sauvages ne sont pas comestibles sous ma forme actuelle.
russian: Как оказалось, некоторые растения для моего текущего обличия не совсем съедобны.
bulgarian: It seems some wild plants are not "edible" in my current form.

english: I will need to proceed with more caution going forward.
french: À partir de maintenant, je vais devoir être plus prudent.
russian: В будущем мне предстоит соблюдать больше осторожности.
bulgarian: I will need to proceed with more caution going forward.

english: A word of advice, [Ari].
french: Un petit conseil, [Ari].
russian: Дам небольшой совет, [Ari].
bulgarian: A word of advice, [Ari].

english: It seems that when I am not actively eating food to sustain myself...
french: Lorsque je ne suis pas en train de consommer de la nourriture pour m'alimenter...
russian: Даже когда я не вкушаю еду, чтобы поддерживать своё тело...
bulgarian: It seems that when I am not actively eating food to sustain myself...

english: I am either gathering it, cooking it, or cleaning it up.
french: Je suis soit en train de la récolter, soit en train de la cuisiner, soit en train de nettoyer.
russian: Я всё равно её либо готовлю, либо убираюсь после трапезы.
bulgarian: I am either gathering it, cooking it, or cleaning it up.

english: Living in this form has certainly been an adjustment.
french: L'existence sous cette forme nécessite un grand effort d'adaptation.
russian: Бытие в этом обличии требует адаптации.
bulgarian: Living in this form has certainly been an adjustment.

english: It seems that one must plan their meals in advance.
french: Il semblerait qu'il faille prévoir ses repas à l'avance.
russian: Видимо, трапезы необходимо планировать заранее.
bulgarian: It seems that one must plan their meals in advance.

english: I waited until I was hungry to go foraging, and found myself fatigued before I was able to gather enough to eat.
french: J'ai attendu d'avoir faim pour me mettre en quête de nourriture et j'ai éprouvé de la fatigue avant d'avoir pu récolter assez à manger.
russian: Я подождал момента, когда проголодаюсь, чтобы пойти собирать плоды. Но я почувствовал усталость прежде, чем собрал достаточно.
bulgarian: I waited until I was hungry to go foraging, and found myself fatigued before I was able to gather enough to eat.

english: I believe it is possible to teleport between them, though I unfortunately do not have the power to do so myself...
french: Je crois qu'il est possible de se téléporter de l'une à l'autre, bien que je n'aie malheureusement pas le pouvoir de le faire moi-même...
russian: Думаю, между ними можно перемещаться... хоть у меня самого такой силы, увы, нет.
bulgarian: Смятам, че е възможно да се телепортираш между тях, но за съжаление аз самият нямам силата да го направя...

english: But perhaps you will find it useful, when you have time to visit.
french: Mais tu trouveras peut-être cela utile, quand tu auras le temps de t'y rendre.
russian: Но, быть может, ты найдёшь в этом пользу, если решишь навестить.
bulgarian: Но може да ти е полезно, когато имаш време да ме посетиш.

english: It seems that there is a connection between the statue in my temple and the one on your farm.
french: Il semblerait qu'une connexion existe entre la statue de mon temple et celle de ta ferme.
russian: Похоже, что статуя в моём храме как-то связана со статуей на твоей ферме.
bulgarian: Изглежда, че има връзка между статуята в храма ми и тази във фермата ти.

english: It seems that some wild plants are not "edible" in my current form.
french: Il semble que certaines plantes sauvages ne soient pas comestibles sous ma forme actuelle.
russian: Как оказалось, некоторые растения для моего текущего обличия не совсем съедобны.
bulgarian: It seems that some wild plants are not "edible" in my current form.

english: I will need to proceed with more caution going forward.
french: À partir de maintenant, je vais devoir être plus prudent.
russian: В будущем мне предстоит соблюдать больше осторожности.
bulgarian: I will need to proceed with more caution going forward.

english: A word of advice, [Ari].
french: Un petit conseil, [Ari].
russian: Дам небольшой совет, [Ari].
bulgarian: A word of advice, [Ari].

english: Having now experienced it firsthand, I can confirm that it is rather unpleasant.
french: Après en avoir fait directement l'expérience, je puis confirmer que c'est assez désagréable.
russian: Теперь, испытав это сам, могу подтвердить: весьма неприятно.
bulgarian: Having now experienced it firsthand, I can confirm that it is rather unpleasant.

english: I had heard tales of humans "stubbing a toe"...
french: J'ai entendu des humains qui parlaient de « se cogner l'orteil »...
russian: Я слышал истории о том, как люди иногда «ударяются мизинцем»...
bulgarian: I had heard tales of humans "stubbing a toe"...

english: More than anything, I enjoy the ingenuity of human textiles. They are most pleasing to the senses.
french: Plus que tout, j'aime l'ingéniosité des tissus humains. Ils sont fort plaisants pour les sens.
russian: Больше всего в человеческих тканях мне нравится находчивость. Настоящая услада чувств.
bulgarian: More than anything, I enjoy the ingenuity of human textiles. They are most pleasing to the senses.

english: This temple was carved directly from stone, and creature comforts were added according to my taste.
french: Ce temple a été sculpté dans la roche, et ses commodités ajoutées selon mes goûts.
russian: Этот храм высечен прямо в скале, а внутреннее обустройство создано по моему вкусу.
bulgarian: This temple was carved directly from stone, and creature comforts were added according to my taste.

english: But as it turns out, a hot drink on a cold day is quite revivifying.
french: Mais il s'avère qu'une boisson chaude quand il fait froid est tout à fait vivifiante.
russian: Но, как оказалось, горячий напиток в холодный день весьма бодрит.
bulgarian: But as it turns out, a hot drink on a cold day is quite revivifying.

english: I once wondered what purpose humans had in boiling leaves.
french: Je me demandais autrefois à quoi il servait aux humains de faire bouillir des feuilles.
russian: Раньше я удивлялся: зачем люди заваривают листья?
bulgarian: I once wondered what purpose humans had in boiling leaves.

english: Ah, good. That is a relief.
french: Ah, très bien. C'est un soulagement.
russian: Ах, хорошо. Вызывает облегчение.
bulgarian: Ah, good. That is a relief.

english: It has been a long time since I have visited the ocean. Is it still salty? Bitterly so?
french: Cela fait bien longtemps que je n'ai pas été dans l'océan. Est-il toujours salé ? Au point d'en être amer ?
russian: Прошло много времени с тех пор, как я бывал у океана. Он всё ещё необычайно солёный?
bulgarian: It has been a long time since I have visited the ocean. Is it still salty? Bitterly so?

english: The salty air, the gentle crashing of the waves... It has been a relief to find them unchanged.
french: L'air iodé, le doux bruit des vagues qui s'écrasent... C'est un soulagement de constater qu'ils n'ont pas changé.
russian: Солёный воздух и плавно накатывающие волны... Какое облегчение, что эти вещи не меняются!
bulgarian: The salty air, the gentle crashing of the waves... It has been a relief to find them unchanged.

english: It is a joy to be able to visit the ocean once more.
french: C'est une joie de pouvoir me rendre à nouveau près de l'océan.
russian: Я так рад, что снова могу побывать у океана.
bulgarian: It is a joy to be able to visit the ocean once more.

english: Is it not marvelous how heat improves a meal?
french: N'est-ce pas merveilleux de voir combien la chaleur améliore un repas ?
russian: Разве не удивительно, как тепло улучшает вкус пищи?
bulgarian: Is it not marvelous how heat improves a meal?

english: Is there a meaning to the paper? Or perhaps the box?
french: Y a-t-il une signification à ce papier ? Ou à cette boîte, peut-être ?
russian: Несёт ли бумага какой-то особенный смысл? Или дело в коробке?
bulgarian: Is there a meaning to the paper? Or perhaps the box?

english: When I was watching over the townsfolk, I saw someone receive a box covered in paper as congratulations for their day of birth. Is this common practice in this era?
french: Alors que je surveillais les villageois, j'ai vu quelqu'un recevoir une boîte recouverte de papier pour fêter le jour de sa naissance. Est-ce une pratique courante dans la région ?
russian: Наблюдая за горожанами, я увидел, как одному вручили завёрнутую в бумагу коробку. В качестве поздравления с днём рождения. Это какой-то распространённый нынче обычай?
bulgarian: When I was watching over the townsfolk, I saw someone receive a box covered in paper as congratulations for their day of birth. Is this common practice in this era?

english: Is there a meaning to the paper? Or perhaps the box?
french: Y a-t-il une signification à ce papier ? Ou à la boîte, peut-être ?
russian: Несёт ли бумага какой-то особенный смысл? Или дело в коробке?
bulgarian: Is there a meaning to the paper? Or perhaps the box?

english: I notice that the villagers will sometimes receive a box covered in paper as congratulations for their day of birth. Is this common practice in this era?
french: J'ai noté que les villageois recevaient parfois une boîte couverte de papier pour fêter le jour de leur naissance. Est-ce une pratique propre à cette époque ?
russian: Иногда я замечаю, как кому-то из горожан вручают завёрнутую в бумагу коробку. В качестве поздравления с днём рождения. Это какой-то распространённый нынче обычай?
bulgarian: I notice that the villagers will sometimes receive a box covered in paper as congratulations for their day of birth. Is this common practice in this era?

english: While a dragon must have horns, it is a shame that they make it impossible to wear any of your delightful human hats.
french: Certes, un dragon doit avoir des cornes, mais il est dommage que cela rende impossible le port de vos ravissants chapeaux humains.
russian: Дракону пристало иметь рога, но, увы, они мешают носить прекрасные человеческие шляпы.
bulgarian: While a dragon must have horns, it is a shame that they make it impossible to wear any of your delightful human hats.

english: I rather enjoy foraging for wild ingredients in the Deep Woods, but I never have enough pockets to store them all.
french: Je trouve assez plaisant de récolter des ingrédients à Boissombre, mais je n'ai jamais assez de poches pour les contenir tous.
russian: Мне по душе собирать дикие ингредиенты в Глубокой чаще, но мне не хватает карманов, чтобы все их унести.
bulgarian: I rather enjoy foraging for wild ingredients in the Deep Woods, but I never have enough pockets to store them all.

english: Thankfully, I rather enjoy decorating my home with lights.
french: Heureusement, cela me plaît assez de décorer ma maison avec des lumières.
russian: К счастью, мне нравится украшать дом огнями.
bulgarian: Thankfully, I rather enjoy decorating my home with lights.

english: I must admit, I am unused to the way my eyes perceive darkness as of late.
french: Je dois avouer que je ne suis pas habitué à la façon dont mes yeux perçoivent l'obscurité, depuis quelque temps.
russian: Признаюсь, я до сих пор не привык к тому, как мои глаза воспринимают тьму.
bulgarian: I must admit, I am unused to the way my eyes perceive darkness as of late.

english: I have recently begun using a pine branch instead of my claws. It is much faster!
french: J'utilise depuis peu une branche de pin plutôt que mes griffes. C'est beaucoup plus rapide !
russian: Недавно я стал использовать сосновую ветку вместо когтей — выходит куда быстрее!
bulgarian: I have recently begun using a pine branch instead of my claws. It is much faster!

english: It smells nice, too.
french: Et puis ça sent bon.
russian: И пахнет приятно.
bulgarian: It smells nice, too.

english: Brushing one's hair takes a surprisingly long time.
french: Se brosser les cheveux prend un temps étonnamment long.
russian: Расчёсывание волос отнимает удивительно много времени.
bulgarian: Brushing one's hair takes a surprisingly long time.

english: Having admired your various ensembles, I have become curious about contemporary attire.
french: En admirant tes différentes tenues, je suis devenu curieux des vêtements contemporains.
russian: Насмотревшись на твои наряды, я начал испытывать любопытство насчёт современной моды.
bulgarian: Having admired your various ensembles, I have become curious about contemporary attire.

english: Someday I should like to walk around this Saturday Market you have spoken of.
french: Un jour, j'aimerais me promener dans ce marché du samedi dont tu m'as parlé.
russian:
Однажды я хотел бы прогуляться по Субботнему базару, о котором ты

рассказывали

рассказываларассказывалрассказывало.
bulgarian: Someday I should like to walk around this Saturday Market you have spoken of.

english: It is quite enjoyable, leisurely browsing each booth.
french: Il est très agréable de contempler à loisir chaque étal.
russian: Неторопливо осматривать разные лавки — весьма приятное занятие.
bulgarian: It is quite enjoyable, leisurely browsing each booth.

english: I should like to walk around the Saturday Market next week.
french: J'aimerais me promener dans le marché du samedi, la semaine prochaine.
russian: На следующей неделе я бы хотел прогуляться по Субботнему базару.
bulgarian: I should like to walk around the Saturday Market next week.

english: Despite my foggy memory, I am thankful my fingers remember how to play the lute.
french: En dépit des brumes de ma mémoire, mes doigts se rappellent heureusement comment jouer du luth.
russian: Несмотря на туман в памяти, к счастью, мои пальцы помнят, как играть на лютне.
bulgarian: Despite my foggy memory, I am thankful my fingers remember how to play the lute.

english: I cannot help but miss the living fire of my draconic form. In this earthly form, I am always at the mercy of the elements.
french: Je ne puis m'empêcher de regretter le feu brûlant de mon existence de dragon. Sous cette forme terrestre, je suis toujours à la merci des éléments.
russian: Я скучаю по живому пламени моего истинного облика. В теле человека я всегда завишу от капризов природы.
bulgarian: I cannot help but miss the living fire of my draconic form. In this earthly form, I am always at the mercy of the elements.

english: Are you not chilled, [Ari]?
french: N'as-tu pas un peu froid, [Ari] ?
russian: Тебе не холодно, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Are you not chilled, [Ari]?

english: Worry not. Beneath these many layers, I am quite comfortable.
french: Mais ne t'inquiète pas, sous ces nombreuses épaisseurs, je me sens à mon aise.
russian: Но не стоит страшиться. Под этими слоями ткани мне достаточно комфортно.
bulgarian: Worry not. Beneath these many layers, I am quite comfortable.

english: I was unprepared for the reality of the elements in a physical form. Now, I must work harder to keep warm.
french: Je n'étais pas préparé à la réalité des éléments sous ma nouvelle forme physique. Désormais, avoir chaud me demande plus de travail.
russian: Я не ожидал, насколько суровы стихии для физической формы. Теперь мне приходится стараться, чтобы согреться.
bulgarian: I was unprepared for the reality of the elements in a physical form. Now, I must work harder to keep warm.

english: In this new shape, I find myself desiring the warmth of company as well.
french: Sous cette nouvelle forme, j'aspire moi-même à la présence chaleureuse de compagnons.
russian: В этой новой форме я желаю теплоты других намного больше.
bulgarian: In this new shape, I find myself desiring the warmth of company as well.

english: Dragons are solitary creatures. Perhaps they would seek company as often as humans do if they were as sensitive to the elements.
french: Les dragons sont des créatures solitaires. Peut-être chercheraient-ils, comme les humains, de la compagnie s'ils étaient aussi sensibles qu'eux aux éléments.
russian: Драконы — одиночки. Вероятно, если бы они были уязвимы к природе так же, как люди, они бы охотнее искали товарищества.
bulgarian: Dragons are solitary creatures. Perhaps they would seek company as often as humans do if they were as sensitive to the elements.

english: Since taking mortal form, I find myself enjoying the warmth of company.
french: Depuis que j'ai pris une forme mortelle, il s'avère que j'apprécie la chaleur d'une compagnie.
russian: Приняв смертное обличье, я нахожу, что стал больше наслаждаться тёплой компанией.
bulgarian: Since taking mortal form, I find myself enjoying the warmth of company.

english: Dragons are typically solitary creatures. However...
french: Les dragons sont généralement des créatures solitaires. Cependant...
russian: Обычно драконы — одиночки. Однако...
bulgarian: Dragons are typically solitary creatures. However...

english: But perhaps they would make it difficult to sleep in my bed.
french: Mais cela serait sans doute plus compliqué pour moi de dormir dans un lit.
russian: Впрочем, они бы мешали мне спать на кровати.
bulgarian: But perhaps they would make it difficult to sleep in my bed.

english: I sometimes wonder if I should have kept my wings in this form...
french: Je me demande parfois si j'aurais dû conserver mes ailes sous cette forme...
russian: Иногда я размышляю, что в этой форме мне стоило сохранить свои крылья...
bulgarian: I sometimes wonder if I should have kept my wings in this form...

english: In my opinion, one can never have enough rugs or blankets.
french: De mon point de vue, on n'a jamais trop de tapis ou de couvertures.
russian: Я считаю, одеял и пледов никогда не может быть слишком много.
bulgarian: In my opinion, one can never have enough rugs or blankets.

english: Of the many and varied human inventions, weaving is one of my favorites. Such meticulous work, and such beautiful results.
french: Des multiples et diverses inventions humaines, le tissage est ma préférée. C'est un travail très méticuleux qui donne de magnifiques résultats.
russian: Из множества изобретений человечества, одно из моих любимых — пряжа. Такая кропотливая работа, но приносит такие прекрасные результаты.
bulgarian: Of the many and varied human inventions, weaving is one of my favorites. Such meticulous work, and such beautiful results.

english: How many rugs is too many?
french: À partir de combien de tapis peut-on dire que l'on en a trop ?
russian: В какой момент пледов становится слишком много?
bulgarian: How many rugs is too many?

english: Looking around my home, one cannot help but wonder...
french: Quand je regarde mon intérieur, une question me vient...
russian: Иногда, осматривая своё жилище, я задумываюсь...
bulgarian: Looking around my home, one cannot help but wonder...

english: Unfortunately, if I were to try them on myself, my talons would certainly rend them to ribbons.
french: Malheureusement, si je devais en passer, elles finiraient sans doute en lambeau à cause de mes griffes.
russian: К сожалению, я не могу испытать этот опыт на себе. Мои когти непременно разорвут их в клочья.
bulgarian: Unfortunately, if I were to try them on myself, my talons would certainly rend them to ribbons.

english: I have always found myself curious about the uniquely human practice of wearing socks.
french: J'ai toujours été intrigué par l'habitude propre aux humains de porter des chaussettes.
russian: Мне всегда было крайне любопытно одно уникальное человеческое свойство — ношение носков.
bulgarian: I have always found myself curious about the uniquely human practice of wearing socks.

english: Perhaps someday, I will try my hand at this... ranching.
french: Peut-être qu'un jour je m'essaierai à cet... élevage.
russian: Возможно, когда-нибудь и мне доведётся попробовать это ваше... животноводство.
bulgarian: Perhaps someday, I will try my hand at this... ranching.

english: The practice of domestication is fascinating. Tying one's future to the beasts of the earth, and vice versa.
french: La pratique de la domestication est fascinante. Il s'agit de lier son destin aux créatures terrestres, et inversement.
russian: Человеческая практика одомашнивания животных впечатляет меня. Есть что-то в этом связывании своей судьбы с другими земными существами.
bulgarian: The practice of domestication is fascinating. Tying one's future to the beasts of the earth, and vice versa.

english: But now, those types of little details seem important.
french: Mais ce genre de petits détails semble désormais important.
russian: А теперь такие мелочи кажутся важными.
bulgarian: But now, those types of little details seem important.

english: In the past, I was never concerned with trimming my claws.
french: Autrefois, je ne me souciais jamais de tailler mes griffes.
russian: Раньше я не задумывался о подрезании когтей.
bulgarian: In the past, I was never concerned with trimming my claws.

english: Yes, it is indeed quite different than mine. It is soft. And warm.
french: Oui, elle est en effet très différente de la mienne. Elle est douce et chaude.
russian: Да уж, она действительно сильно отличается от моей. Такая мягкая. И теплая.
bulgarian: Yes, it is indeed quite different than mine. It is soft. And warm.

english: [Ari]. A matter of curiosity, I would like to see your hand if you would not mind.
french: [Ari]. Par pure curiosité, j'aimerais regarder ta main, si cela ne t'ennuie pas.
russian: [Ari], позволь мне утолить любопытсво. Покажи свою руку, если тебя это не затруднит.
bulgarian: [Ari]. A matter of curiosity, I would like to see your hand if you would not mind.

english: I hope my stature does not trouble you.
french: J'espère que ma stature ne te dérange pas.
russian: Надеюсь, мой рост не доставляет тебе неудобств.
bulgarian: I hope my stature does not trouble you.

english: I did not intend to become notably taller than the average human when I transformed.
french: Quand je me suis transformé, il n'était pas dans mon intention de devenir beaucoup plus grand que la plupart des êtres humains.
russian: Я не преследовал цели стать заметно выше других людей, когда принимал эту форму.
bulgarian: I did not intend to become notably taller than the average human when I transformed.

english: What is the experience of wearing shoes like? Do you wear them for protection, or for self-expression?
french: Qu'éprouve-t-on lorsque l'on porte des chaussures ? Le fait-on pour se protéger ou est-ce un moyen d'exprimer qui l'on est ?
russian: Каково это — носить обувь? Вы, люди, носите её для защиты ног или просто для самовыражения?
bulgarian: What is the experience of wearing shoes like? Do you wear them for protection, or for self-expression?

english: And so, humans perplex me. Is it not difficult to move around without one?
french: Par conséquent, les humains me laissent perplexe. N'est-il pas difficile de se déplacer sans cela ?
russian: Потому я не понимаю, как люди обходятся без него. Разве это не трудно?
bulgarian: And so, humans perplex me. Is it not difficult to move around without one?

english: I have always considered a tail essential for balance.
french: J'ai toujours considéré qu'avoir une queue était indispensable à l'équilibre.
russian: Хвост всегда казался мне необходимым для равновесия.
bulgarian: I have always considered a tail essential for balance.

english: The anticipation of a meal nearly ready to eat. The anticipation of unfurling a scroll. The anticipation of your next visit.
french: L'impatience devant un repas presque prêt à manger. L'impatience de dérouler un parchemin. L'impatience de ta prochaine visite.
russian: Предвкушение трапезы, когда блюдо почти готово. Приятное ожидание, когда разворачиваешь свиток. Предвкушение твоего визита.
bulgarian: The anticipation of a meal nearly ready to eat. The anticipation of unfurling a scroll. The anticipation of your next visit.

english: It is new to me.
french: Tout cela est nouveau pour moi.
russian: Для меня всё это в новинку.
bulgarian: It is new to me.

english: Somehow, feelings are sharper and more pronounced lately.
french: Curieusement, j'éprouve des sentiments plus nets et plus forts depuis quelque temps.
russian: В последнее время чувства стали острее и ярче.
bulgarian: Somehow, feelings are sharper and more pronounced lately.

english: I thought that the priestesses looked so elegant with their tresses. And they made it look so easy...
french: Je trouvais les prêtresses si élégantes avec leurs tresses. Et cela avait l'air si simple à faire...
russian: Жрицы с пышными косами казались мне такими изящными. Будто это им давалось так легко...
bulgarian: I thought that the priestesses looked so elegant with their tresses. And they made it look so easy...

english: They never came to the temple with leaves caught in a tangle.
french: Jamais elles ne venaient au temple avec des feuilles coincées dans une tignasse emmêlée.
russian: Они никогда не приходили в храм с листьями, запутавшимися в прядях.
bulgarian: They never came to the temple with leaves caught in a tangle.

english: When I chose this form, I did not realize just how much one must care for hair. Dragons need not worry about such things.
french: Quand j'ai choisi cette forme, je n'ai pas réalisé combien il fallait prendre soin de sa chevelure. Les dragons n'ont nul besoin de s'inquiéter de telles choses.
russian: Выбирая эту форму, я не осознавал, сколько забот доставляют волосы. Драконам не приходится о таком думать.
bulgarian: When I chose this form, I did not realize just how much one must care for hair. Dragons need not worry about such things.

english: It would be nice to experience the bathhouse, one day. A hot bath now holds a great deal of appeal.
french: J'apprécierais d'essayer les bains, un jour. L'idée de me plonger dans une eau chauffée me semble désormais très attrayante.
russian: Хотелось бы однажды попробовать купальню. Горячая ванна теперь кажется очень заманчивой.
bulgarian: It would be nice to experience the bathhouse, one day. A hot bath now holds a great deal of appeal.

english: Bathing in a stream is natural for a dragon, but the water is colder than I remember.
french: Se baigner dans un cours d'eau est naturel pour un dragon, mais l'eau est plus froide que dans mon souvenir.
russian: Купание в ручье — естественно для дракона, но вода оказалась холоднее, чем я помнил.
bulgarian: Bathing in a stream is natural for a dragon, but the water is colder than I remember.

english: A hot bath holds a great deal more appeal. I am thankful that I may now visit the bathhouse as I please.
french: Un bain chaud a beaucoup plus d'attraits. Je suis reconnaissant de pouvoir désormais me rendre aux bains comme bon me semble.
russian: Горячая ванна гораздо привлекательнее. Благодарю тебя за то, что теперь могу посещать купальню, когда пожелаю.
bulgarian: A hot bath holds a great deal more appeal. I am thankful that I may now visit the bathhouse as I please.

english: Bathing in a stream is natural for a dragon, but the water is rather cold...
french: Se baigner dans un cours d'eau est naturel pour un dragon, mais l'eau est plutôt froide...
russian: Купание в ручье — естественно для дракона, но вода довольно холодная...
bulgarian: Bathing in a stream is natural for a dragon, but the water is rather cold...

english: I was able to purchase a packet of grounds, which I brewed this morning.
bulgarian: I was able to purchase a packet of grounds, which I brewed this morning.

english: An anonymous request of Balor secured me a packet of grounds, which I brewed this morning.
french: Grâce à une demande anonyme auprès de Balor, j'ai pu en obtenir un paquet moulu, que j'ai fait infuser ce matin.
russian: По анонимной просьбе Балор доставил мне пакет молотых зёрен. Я заварил его сегодня утром.
bulgarian: An anonymous request of Balor secured me a packet of grounds, which I brewed this morning.

english: However, I believe my measurements may have been off. Unless, the room seems to be vibrating to you as well...?
french: Il me semble cependant que mon dosage était inapproprié. Sauf s'il te semble, à toi aussi, que la pièce tremble...?
russian: Однако, подозреваю, я переборщил с дозировкой. Или для тебя эта комната тоже ходит ходуном?...
bulgarian: However, I believe my measurements may have been off. Unless, the room seems to be vibrating to you as well...?

english: Since awakening, I have observed many in Mistria drinking a beverage extracted from fire-darkened beans. They called it... $Coffee$.
french: Depuis que je me suis réveillé, j'ai constaté que beaucoup de personnes à Mistria consommaient un breuvage extrait de fèves noircies au feu. Elles appellent cela... café.
russian: Со времени моего пробуждения я заметил, что в Мистрии пьют напиток из обжаренных зёрен. Его называют... кофе.
bulgarian: Since awakening, I have observed many in Mistria drinking a beverage extracted from fire-darkened beans. They called it... $Coffee$.

english: But now, I must admit... it is pleasing to express oneself through clothing.
french: Mais désormais, je dois l'avouer... Il est agréable de s'exprimer par l'habillement.
russian: Но теперь, признаю... приятно выражать себя с помощью одежды.
bulgarian: But now, I must admit... it is pleasing to express oneself through clothing.

english: As a dragon, I did not wear any adornments save the ceremonial necessities.
french: Sous ma forme de dragon, je ne portais aucune parure, hormis pour les obligations cérémonielles.
russian: Будучи драконом, я не носил никаких украшений, кроме церемониальных.
bulgarian: As a dragon, I did not wear any adornments save the ceremonial necessities.

english: It has inspired me to grow my own garden as well.
french: Cela m'a motivé à faire moi aussi mon propre jardin.
russian: ...Я и сам вдохновился на выращивание собственного сада.
bulgarian: It has inspired me to grow my own garden as well.

english: All that time, watching the plants grow so happily on your farm...
french: Tout ce temps passé à regarder les plantes pousser avec tant de bonheur sur ta ferme...
russian: За всё время наблюдения, как счастливо растения сосуществуют на твоей ферме...
bulgarian: All that time, watching the plants grow so happily on your farm...

english: They are growing up well.
french: Ils poussent bien.
russian: Они хорошо растут.
bulgarian: They are growing up well.

english: Greetings, [Ari]. I was just conversing with the little ones here.
french: Félicitations, [Ari]. J'étais en train de converser avec ces petits plants.
russian: Приветствую, [Ari]. Я всего лишь общался с этими малютками.
bulgarian: Greetings, [Ari]. I was just conversing with the little ones here.

english: I understand you a little more, I think.
french: Je crois que je te comprends un peu mieux.
russian: Кажется, я стал понимать тебя чуточку лучше.
bulgarian: I understand you a little more, I think.

english: Turning the earth over with my own hands, readying it for planting...
french: Retourner la terre de mes mains, la préparer pour les semis...
russian: Собственными руками пахая землю и подготавливая её к посадке растений...
bulgarian: Turning the earth over with my own hands, readying it for planting...

english: It is a blessing that the soil gifts us with crops, no matter the season.
french: C'est une bénédiction que le sol nous fasse cadeau de ses récoltes, quelle que soit la saison.
russian: Как благословенно, что земля может одарить нас урожаем независимо от времени года.
bulgarian: It is a blessing that the soil gifts us with crops, no matter the season.

english: It is much better than using my claws.
french: C'est bien mieux que d'utiliser mes griffes.
russian: Использовать её намного удобнее, чем собственные когти.
bulgarian: It is much better than using my claws.

english: I am thankful that Balor was able to procure a spade in one of my orders.
french: Je suis reconnaissant à Balor d'avoir pu se procurer la bêche que j'avais demandée dans l'une de mes commandes.
russian: Я благодарен Балору, что он смог доставить мне мотыгу по моему заказу.
bulgarian: I am thankful that Balor was able to procure a spade in one of my orders.

english: Rather, the plants tell me what they need as they need it.
french: Ce sont plutôt les plantes qui me disent au fur et à mesure ce dont elles ont besoin.
russian: Они сами сообщают мне, что и когда им необходимо.
bulgarian: Rather, the plants tell me what they need as they need it.

english: I do not keep a regular schedule of watering the way that you do.
french: Je ne tiens pas, comme toi, un calendrier régulier des arrosages.
russian: В отличие от тебя, я не придерживаюсь регулярного расписания, когда поливаю растения.
bulgarian: I do not keep a regular schedule of watering the way that you do.

english: It makes gardening in the Deep Woods a challenge. And yet, it is an enjoyable one.
french: Cela fait du jardinage à Boissombre un défi, néanmoins plaisant.
russian: По этой причине садоводство в Глубокой чаще не из лёгких. Но трудности делают это лишь интереснее.
bulgarian: It makes gardening in the Deep Woods a challenge. And yet, it is an enjoyable one.

english: The elder trees here have first claim of nutrients in the soil, as well as sunlight.
french: Les arbres les plus anciens ont été les premiers à prétendre aux nutriments du sol et à la lumière du soleil.
russian: Старинные деревья в этом лесу по праву первыми питаются от земли и солнца.
bulgarian: The elder trees here have first claim of nutrients in the soil, as well as sunlight.

english: Maybe someday I will have the opportunity to do some planting there.
french: Peut-être aurai-je un jour l'opportunité d'y faire quelques plantations.
russian: Возможно, придёт день, когда мне представится возможность посадить что-нибудь и там.
bulgarian: Maybe someday I will have the opportunity to do some planting there.

english: Near the statue bearing my likeness, perhaps.
french: Pourquoi pas près de la statue qui me ressemble ?
russian: Возможно, рядом со статуей по моему образу.
bulgarian: Near the statue bearing my likeness, perhaps.

english: I would be curious to see how the soil in the Deep Woods differs from your farm, [Ari].
french: Je serais curieux de voir ce qui distingue le sol de Boissombre de celui de ta ferme, [Ari].
russian: Мне было бы интересно узнать, чем почва Глубокой чащи отличается от твоей, [Ari], на ферме.
bulgarian: I would be curious to see how the soil in the Deep Woods differs from your farm, [Ari].

english: I wish to replicate it, but the letters are worn from age and water damage.
french: J'aimerais la reproduire, mais les caractères sont difficiles à lire, décolorés par l'humidité et l'ancienneté.
russian: Я бы хотел его воспроизвести, но буквы затёрлись от времени и влаги.
bulgarian: I wish to replicate it, but the letters are worn from age and water damage.

english: Do you suppose it calls for two scoops of sugar, or two bags?
french: D'après toi, a-t-on besoin de deux cuillères ou de deux sacs de sucre ?
russian: Как ты полагаешь, там требуется две ложки сахара или два мешка?
bulgarian: Do you suppose it calls for two scoops of sugar, or two bags?

english: I will use two bags, just to be certain.
french: Je vais en mettre deux sacs, par sécurité.
russian: Лучше положу два мешка. На всякий случай.
bulgarian: I will use two bags, just to be certain.

english: I came across a curious recipe in an old tome...
french: J'ai découvert une curieuse recette dans un vieil ouvrage...
russian: Я нашёл в одном старом фолианте любопытный рецепт...
bulgarian: I came across a curious recipe in an old tome...

english: However, when speaking with Reina about cooking, she says it is a creative endeavor with no wrong answers.
french: Néanmoins, quand je parle de cuisine avec Reina, elle affirme qu'il s'agit d'un processus créatif où il n'y a jamais de mauvaise réponse.
russian: А когда я говорю про готовку с Рейной, она говорит, что это творческий процесс, где нет неправильных ответов.
bulgarian: However, when speaking with Reina about cooking, she says it is a creative endeavor with no wrong answers.

english: They are not unlike philosophers from different schools of thought. I will endeavor to learn from them both.
french: Ils m'évoquent deux philosophes suivant des écoles de pensée différentes. Je vais m'efforcer d'apprendre de chacun d'eux.
russian: В этом они напоминают мне философов разных школ. И я буду стремиться усвоить уроки от них обоих.
bulgarian: They are not unlike philosophers from different schools of thought. I will endeavor to learn from them both.

english: When I converse with Ryis about baking, he describes it as a precise science with specific measurements, temperatures, and timing.
french: Quand je discute avec Ryis de la cuisson, il en parle comme d'une science exacte, avec des mesures, des températures et une durée précises.
russian: Когда я обсуждаю выпечку с Ризом, он описывает её как строгую науку с точными измерениями, температурой и отсчётом времени.
bulgarian: When I converse with Ryis about baking, he describes it as a precise science with specific measurements, temperatures, and timing.

english: I have great appreciation and admiration for Balor... he fulfilled my orders while I was confined to the Deep Woods...
french: J'apprécie Balor et je l'admire beaucoup... Il a honoré mes commandes lorsque j'étais confiné à Boissombre...
russian: Я высоко ценю и уважаю Балора... Он выполнял мои заказы, когда я был заперт в Глубокой чаще...
bulgarian: I have great appreciation and admiration for Balor... he fulfilled my orders while I was confined to the Deep Woods...

english: But if one desires to make cookies today, one needs $Chocolate$ with great urgency.
french: Mais pour préparer des cookies aujourd'hui, du $chocolat$ va m'être nécessaire de toute urgence.
russian: Но если вдруг захочется сегодня же сделать печенье, $шоколад$ необходимо добыть немедленно.
bulgarian: But if one desires to make cookies today, one needs $Chocolate$ with great urgency.

english: It is wonderful, being able to walk to a grocery store to buy what I need right away.
french: Il est merveilleux de pouvoir se rendre à pied jusqu'à une épicerie pour acheter immédiatement ce dont j'ai besoin.
russian: Как же чудесно иметь возможность зайти в магазин и сразу купить всё, что мне нужно.
bulgarian: It is wonderful, being able to walk to a grocery store to buy what I need right away.

english: As the years pass, the tree lifts the marker skyward.
french: Au fil des ans, la tablette s'élève à mesure que l'arbre pousse.
russian: Год за годом дерево поднимает плиту наверх.
bulgarian: As the years pass, the tree lifts the marker skyward.

english: Over time, the headstone becomes too high for the average person to read, as is the case with the grave of Doctor Valen's father.
french: Petit à petit, la stèle devient trop haute pour être lue par la plupart des gens, comme c'est le cas pour la sépulture du père de la docteure Valen.
russian: Со временем она оказывается так высоко, что обычный человек уже не может её прочитать. Так случилось с погребальной плитой отца Вален.
bulgarian: Over time, the headstone becomes too high for the average person to read, as is the case with the grave of Doctor Valen's father.

english: Soon, even I will not be able to read its epitaph.
french: Bientôt, même moi je ne pourrai plus lire son épitaphe.
russian: Скоро даже я не смогу прочитать эпитафию.
bulgarian: Soon, even I will not be able to read its epitaph.

english: Mistrians have long held the tradition of attaching burial markers to young saplings.
french: Les Mistriens ont pour tradition, depuis longtemps, d'attacher des tablettes funéraires à des arbrisseaux.
russian: У мистрийцев есть древняя традиция прицеплять к молодым росткам погребальные плиты.
bulgarian: Mistrians have long held the tradition of attaching burial markers to young saplings.

english: It is curious to know so much of her, despite never having the opportunity to meet her.
french: Il est curieux de connaître d'elle tant de choses sans jamais avoir eu l'occasion de la rencontrer.
russian: Занимательно, как много я о ней знаю, хотя ни разу её не видел.
bulgarian: It is curious to know so much of her, despite never having the opportunity to meet her.

english: Yet, she is ever-present. In Hayden's home, and his mannerisms, and his person.
french: Pourtant, elle est toujours présente. Dans la maison d'Hayden, dans ses habitudes, dans sa gestuelle.
russian: Тем не менее она незримо присутствует с нами. В доме Хейдена, в его повадках и в его характере.
bulgarian: Yet, she is ever-present. In Hayden's home, and his mannerisms, and his person.

english: Hayden's storied grandmother is laid to rest in this grove.
french: La légendaire grand-mère d'Hayden repose dans ce bosquet.
russian: В этой роще покоится бабушка Хейдена — героиня многих историй.
bulgarian: Hayden's storied grandmother is laid to rest in this grove.

english: But in the winter, the snow hushes all sound...
french: Mais en hiver, la neige étouffe tous les sons...
russian: А зимой снег приглушает все звуки...
bulgarian: But in the winter, the snow hushes all sound...

english: And that quiet becomes deeper, and enveloping.
french: Et le calme s'approfondit encore, devient plus enveloppant.
russian: И тишина становится ещё более глубокой и всепроникающей.
bulgarian: And that quiet becomes deeper, and enveloping.

english: Almost like a touch.
french: Presque palpable.
russian: В такие моменты она кажется почти осязаемой.
bulgarian: Almost like a touch.

english: The Grove of Rest is always a place of quiet contemplation.
french: Le bosquet du repos est toujours un lieu de contemplation paisible.
russian: Роща упокоения — это всегда место для размышлений в тишине.
bulgarian: The Grove of Rest is always a place of quiet contemplation.

english: The towering pines are singularly beautiful when capped in snow.
french: Ces immenses pins sont d'une singulière beauté lorsque la neige les coiffe.
russian: Эти величавые сосны необыкновенно прекрасны в своих снежных шапках.
bulgarian: The towering pines are singularly beautiful when capped in snow.

english: Ah, [Ari]... Have you also come to appreciate the grove's winter raiment?
french: Ah, [Ari]... Es-tu là pour savourer la parure hivernale de ces bois ?
russian:
А, [Ari]... Ты тоже

пришли

пришлапришёлпришло полюбоваться зимним одеянием рощи?
bulgarian: Ah, [Ari]... Have you also come to appreciate the grove's winter raiment?

english: Observing Henrietta... I am reminded of these stories.
french: Et regarder Henrietta... me rappelle ces contes.
russian: Когда я наблюдаю за Генриеттой... Я вспоминаю эти рассказы.
bulgarian: Observing Henrietta... I am reminded of these stories.

english: There were tales I was told as a hatchling, of prehistoric terrorbirds so great and fierce they could overtake an unsuspecting young dragon.
french: Quand j'étais tout petit, on m'a raconté des histoires d'oiseaux préhistoriques terrifiants, si grands et redoutables qu'ils pouvaient emporter un jeune dragon.
russian: Когда я только вылупился, мне рассказывали легенды о грозных доисторических птицах. Они были такие огромные и свирепые, что могли сразить зазевавшегося молодого дракона.
bulgarian: There were tales I was told as a hatchling, of prehistoric terrorbirds so great and fierce they could overtake an unsuspecting young dragon.

english: Her sense of humor is quite cutting, however. I hope she will learn to temper her wit as she matures.
french: Mais elle a un sens de l'humour assez incisif. J'espère qu'elle apprendra à modérer ses traits d'esprit quand elle gagnera en maturité.
russian: Однако у неё весьма едкое чувство юмора. Надеюсь, с возрастом она научится сдерживать свои остроты.
bulgarian: Her sense of humor is quite cutting, however. I hope she will learn to temper her wit as she matures.

english: Hayden's chicken, Henrietta, seems more clever than the rest of her flock...
french: Henrietta, la poule d'Hayden, semble plus maligne que ses congénères...
russian: Генриетта, курица Хейдена, кажется умнее своих собратьев...
bulgarian: Hayden's chicken, Henrietta, seems more clever than the rest of her flock...

english: It resonates with those who hold the affections of their animals.
french: Elle entre en résonance avec les personnes pour qui leurs animaux ont de l'affection.
russian: Она откликается тем, кто с любовью относится к животным.
bulgarian: It resonates with those who hold the affections of their animals.

english: Love is an old and enduring magic, indeed.
french: L'amour est bien une forme de magie ancienne et durable.
russian: Ведь любовь — это магия, не увядающая с самых древних времён.
bulgarian: Love is an old and enduring magic, indeed.

english: There is old magic flowing through the statue south of this farm...
french: Une magie ancienne émane de la statue située au sud de cette ferme...
russian: Статуя к югу от этой фермы хранит древнюю магию...
bulgarian: There is old magic flowing through the statue south of this farm...

english: Watching him tend to the animals is quite calming, and he never fails to send me off with a homecooked meal.
french: Le regarder s'occuper de ses animaux est très apaisant et je repars toujours chez moi avec un repas maison.
russian: Я наполняюсь спокойствием, когда вижу, как он ухаживает за животными. И он всегда даёт мне домашней еды в дорогу.
bulgarian: Watching him tend to the animals is quite calming, and he never fails to send me off with a homecooked meal.

english: I wonder if he considers me another beast to mind...
french: Je me demande s'il me considère comme une créature sur laquelle il doit veiller...
russian: Мне пришло в голову: может, он заботится обо мне, как о ещё одном чудном звере...
bulgarian: I wonder if he considers me another beast to mind...

english: Hayden has welcomed my visits to his farm most graciously.
french: Hayden accueille de bonne grâce mes visites dans sa ferme.
russian: Хейден всегда крайне любезно принимает меня в гостях.
bulgarian: Hayden has welcomed my visits to his farm most graciously.

english: They are quite sweet, if you are partial to sweetness.
french: Elles sont très sucrées, pour qui est friand de ce goût.
russian: Если тебе нравятся сладости, то вкус этих ягод придётся тебе по нраву.
bulgarian: They are quite sweet, if you are partial to sweetness.

english: Have you seen the $Bell Berries$ growing around the Deep Woods?
french: As-tu vu les $clocherelles$ qui poussent un peu partout à Boissombre ?
russian: Представлялось ли тебе видать в сей Глубокой чаще $колокольник$?
bulgarian: Have you seen the $Bell Berries$ growing around the Deep Woods?

english: Do not be confused. They are not true dragons.
french: Ne laisse pas leur nom t'embrouiller : leurs cornes sont minuscules.
russian: Не стоит путать их с настоящими драконами.
bulgarian: Do not be confused. They are not true dragons.

english: The $Dragon Horn Beetle$ can occasionally be found in these woods.
french: On trouve parfois dans ces bois des $corneléoptère$.
russian: Иногда в этих лесах можно встретить $жука-драконорога$.
bulgarian: The $Dragon Horn Beetle$ can occasionally be found in these woods.

english: Have you seen the $Mote Firefly$? There is a legend that they appear in great times of need, when a lost traveler must be guided from the woods.
french: As-tu déjà vu une $luciole des bois$ ? La légende veut qu'elles apparaissent dans les moments de grande détresse, pour guider hors des bois les voyageurs perdus.
russian: Доводилось ли тебе встречать $светлячка-крошку$? По легенде, эти создания объявляются во время великой нужды, чтобы вывести потерявшегося путника из леса.
bulgarian: Have you seen the $Mote Firefly$? There is a legend that they appear in great times of need, when a lost traveler must be guided from the woods.

english: One never knows when the opportunity for a duet might arise.
french: On ne sait jamais quand pourrait se présenter l'occasion d'un duo.
russian: Никогда не знаешь, когда тебе может представиться возможность сыграть дуэтом.
bulgarian: One never knows when the opportunity for a duet might arise.

english: It is rare to hear the $Singing Katydid$ in these woods, but I like to keep my lute close at hand just in case.
french: Il est rare d'entendre la $locuste chantante$ dans ces bois, mais j'aime garder mon luth à portée de main, au cas où.
russian: Услышать $певчего длинноуса$ в этих лесах — возможность редкая. Но я предпочитаю держать лютню при себе. На всякий случай.
bulgarian: It is rare to hear the $Singing Katydid$ in these woods, but I like to keep my lute close at hand just in case.

english: They are beautiful, and make a pleasant =Spirit Mushroom Tea=.
french: Ils sont magnifiques et permettent de préparer un =thé aux cérébolets= délicieux.
russian: Они красиво выглядят, а =чай из призрачных грибов= приятен на вкус.
bulgarian: They are beautiful, and make a pleasant =Spirit Mushroom Tea=.

english: Have you foraged any $Spirit Mushrooms$ yet?
french: As-tu déjà récolté des $cérébolets$ ?
russian: Попадались ли тебе $призрачные грибы$?
bulgarian: Have you foraged any $Spirit Mushrooms$ yet?

english: I am pleased to see they have lasted through the ages.
french: Je suis ravi qu'ils aient survécu au fil des époques.
russian: Меня радует, что даже спустя века они всё ещё цветут.
bulgarian: I am pleased to see they have lasted through the ages.

english: The Priestesses loved the $Temple Flowers$ that grew in the Deep Woods, and planted them around the temple grounds.
french: Les prêtresses adoraient les $plumeria$ qui poussaient à Boissombre et en ont planté partout autour du temple.
russian: Жрицы очень любили $храмовые цветы$, что росли в Глубокой чаще, и рассадили их вокруг территории храма.
bulgarian: The Priestesses loved the $Temple Flowers$ that grew in the Deep Woods, and planted them around the temple grounds.

english: You must be careful when harvesting $Thorn Vines$, [Ari]. Their barbs are difficult to navigate, even if one has claws.
french: Fais bien attention quand tu récoltes des $ronces$, [Ari]. Il est difficile d'éviter leurs épines, même quand on a des griffes.
russian: Тебе следует соблюдать осторожность, собирая $шипастые лозы$, [Ari]. Даже для когтей их шипы доставляют много неудобств.
bulgarian: You must be careful when harvesting $Thorn Vines$, [Ari]. Their barbs are difficult to navigate, even if one has claws.

english: If you need help cracking them open, I am happy to oblige.
french: Si tu as besoin d'aide pour les casser et les ouvrir, je te rendrai ce service avec plaisir.
russian: Если тебе понадобится помощь в их колке, я буду рад её оказать.
bulgarian: If you need help cracking them open, I am happy to oblige.

english: $Walnuts$ grow quite plentifully in the Deep Woods.
french: Il y a énormément de $noix$ à Boissombre.
russian: В Глубокой чаще растёт много $грецких орехов$.
bulgarian: $Walnuts$ grow quite plentifully in the Deep Woods.

english: It is an ancient custom, to plant a tree when a human passes on.
french: C'est une coutume très ancienne de planter un arbre quand un humain trépasse.
russian: По древней традиции, когда человек уходит из этого мира, в этой роще сажается дерево.
bulgarian: It is an ancient custom, to plant a tree when a human passes on.

english: A stone marker is attached to the sapling at the burial site, allowing the stone to integrate and grow upward with the tree over time...
french: Sur le lieu de la sépulture, on fixe une tablette de pierre sur la jeune pousse. Cette tablette fait corps avec l'arbre et s'élève lorsque celui-ci grandit...
russian: На месте погребения к ростку дерева прикрепляется каменная плита, и когда дерево вырастает, плита поднимается ввысь вместе с ним.
bulgarian: A stone marker is attached to the sapling at the burial site, allowing the stone to integrate and grow upward with the tree over time...

english: It represents the ascension of the spirit into its next life.
french: Cela représente l'ascension de l'esprit vers sa prochaine vie.
russian: Это символизирует восхождение духа в новую жизнь.
bulgarian: It represents the ascension of the spirit into its next life.

english: The $Grove of Rest$ lies to the west of here.
french: Le $bosquet du repos$ se trouve à l'ouest d'ici.
russian: К западу отсюда лежит $Роща упокоения$.
bulgarian: The $Grove of Rest$ lies to the west of here.

english: The Dragon Priestesses truly were diligent record keepers.
bulgarian: The Dragon Priestesses truly were diligent record keepers.

english: It seems that the Dragon Priestesses were diligent record keepers.
french: On dirait que les prêtresses dragon étaient des archivistes minutieuses.
russian: По видимому, жрицы прилежно вели записи.
bulgarian: It seems that the Dragon Priestesses were diligent record keepers.

english: I am grateful. Reading these has helped me to piece together events that occurred while I slept.
bulgarian: I am grateful. Reading these has helped me to piece together events that occurred while I slept.

english: I am grateful. I hope that by reading these, I can piece together the gaps in my memory.
french: Je leur en suis reconnaissant. J'espère qu'en les lisant, je pourrai combler les lacunes de ma mémoire.
russian: Я благодарен им за это. Надеюсь, прочитав эти записи, я смогу восполнить пробелы в воспоминаниях.
bulgarian: I am grateful. I hope that by reading these, I can piece together the gaps in my memory.

english: All of these old scrolls...
french: Tous ces vieux parchemins...
russian: Сколько здесь древних свитков...
bulgarian: All of these old scrolls...

english: "A civilization predating the Alda constructed the exterior areas prior to the Dark Ages, but the cave itself existed long before that."
french: « Une civilisation antérieure à Alda a édifié les parties extérieures avant les âges obscurs, mais la grotte elle-même existait bien avant cela. »
russian: «Цивилизация, что старше Альды, возвела внешние стены храма до наступления Тёмных веков, но внутренняя пещера существует ещё дольше».
bulgarian: "A civilization predating the Alda constructed the exterior areas prior to the Dark Ages, but the cave itself existed long before that."

english: I understand now that the "Dark Ages" described were triggered by my decision to seal Seridia.
bulgarian: I understand now that the "Dark Ages" described were triggered by my decision to seal Seridia.

english: I am not familiar with the "Dark Ages" mentioned.
french: Je ne sais pas ce que sont les « âges obscurs » qui sont mentionnés.
russian: Термин «Тёмные века» мне не знаком.
bulgarian: I am not familiar with the "Dark Ages" mentioned.

english: Perhaps I missed it...?
french: Peut-être les ai-je manqués... ?
russian: Вероятно, я их пропустил...
bulgarian: Perhaps I missed it...?

english: It is not pleasant reading, but there is future benefit to understanding the unintended ramifications of one's actions...
bulgarian: It is not pleasant reading, but there is future benefit to understanding the unintended ramifications of one's actions...

english: Perhaps I missed it...?
french: Peut-être les ai-je manqués...?
bulgarian: Perhaps I missed it...?

english: I am currently reading a scroll about the history of this temple.
french: Je lis actuellement un parchemin sur l'histoire de ce temple.
russian: Я в процессе чтения свитка об истории этого храма.
bulgarian: I am currently reading a scroll about the history of this temple.

english: It seems that the "Alda civilization" mentioned was formed from fragmented tribes at the end of the Dark Ages.
french: Il semblerait que la « civilisation d'Alda » qu'ils évoquent ait été constituée de tribus éparpillées à la fin des âges obscurs.
russian: Судя по прочитанному, упомянутая «Альдийская цивилизация» сформировалась в конце Тёмных веков из разрозненных племён.
bulgarian: It seems that the "Alda civilization" mentioned was formed from fragmented tribes at the end of the Dark Ages.

english: Strangely, I can find no records that they had queens, kings, or any nobility at all.
french: Bizarrement, je n'ai trouvé aucune trace de l'existence de reines, de rois ou de nobles.
russian: Это странно, но я не смог найти никаких записей про их правителей, королев или вообще о какой-нибудь знати.
bulgarian: Strangely, I can find no records that they had queens, kings, or any nobility at all.

english: I vaguely recall that queens ruled the human tribes at one time. How mysterious...
french: Je me souviens vaguement qu'à une époque, des reines dirigeaient les tribus humaines. C'est très mystérieux...
russian: Смутно, но я припоминаю: было время, когда человеческими племенами правили королевы. Как загадочно...
bulgarian: I vaguely recall that queens ruled the human tribes at one time. How mysterious...

english: I have been recovering much information from these old scrolls.
french: Ces vieux parchemins m'ont fourni beaucoup d'informations.
russian: Я узнаю очень много информации из здешных свитков.
bulgarian: I have been recovering much information from these old scrolls.

english: I understand that the "Alda civilization" was formed from fragmented tribes at the end of the Dark Ages.
bulgarian: I understand that the "Alda civilization" was formed from fragmented tribes at the end of the Dark Ages.

english: Those fragmented tribes consisted of commoners once ruled by Seridia, before she was sealed.
bulgarian: Those fragmented tribes consisted of commoners once ruled by Seridia, before she was sealed.

english: When $Magic$ disappeared, noble society collapsed. Seridia's court fled east in search of me, hoping to form a new dragon pact to restore their power.
bulgarian: When $Magic$ disappeared, noble society collapsed. Seridia's court fled east in search of me, hoping to form a new dragon pact to restore their power.

english: Perhaps that is why the lands to the east became known as the $Caldosian Empire$.
bulgarian: Perhaps that is why the lands to the east became known as the $Caldosian Empire$.

english: Somehow, that raises more questions than it answers.
bulgarian: Somehow, that raises more questions than it answers.

english: I have been learning much from these old scrolls.
bulgarian: I have been learning much from these old scrolls.

english: Finally, a scroll referencing the queens that ruled the human tribes prior to the Dark Ages.
french: Enfin, un rouleau de parchemin fait référence aux reines qui dirigeaient les tribus humaines avant les âges obscurs.
russian: Я наконец нашёл свиток, в котором упоминаются королевы, правивщие человеческими племенами до наступления Тёмных веков.
bulgarian: Finally, a scroll referencing the queens that ruled the human tribes prior to the Dark Ages.

english: The timeline surrounding my long slumber is starting to slot into place but...
french: La chronologie entourant mon long sommeil commence à se mettre en place, mais...
russian: Я начинаю понимать, как шло время пока я был погружен в глубокий сон, но...
bulgarian: The timeline surrounding my long slumber is starting to slot into place but...

english: What happened, I wonder?
french: Je me demande ce qu'il s'est passé.
russian: Что же всё-таки произошло?
bulgarian: What happened, I wonder?

english: I wish that I could remember more. I must continue my research.
french: Si seulement je me souvenais de plus de choses. Je dois poursuivre mes recherches.
russian: Мне хотелось бы вспомнить больше. Необходимо продолжать исследования.
bulgarian: I wish that I could remember more. I must continue my research.

english: [Ari]! I have uncovered something most interesting.
french: [Ari] ! J'ai découvert quelque chose de très intéressant.
russian: [Ari]! Я разузнал кое-что крайне интересное.
bulgarian: [Ari]! I have uncovered something most interesting.

english: "The Caldosians and the Aldarians are known to share a common ancestral origin."
french: « On sait que les Caldosiens et les Aldariens partagent une origine commune. »
russian: «Кальдосийцы и альдарийцы имеют общих предков».
bulgarian: "The Caldosians and the Aldarians are known to share a common ancestral origin."

english: Caldosians... and the Aldarians.
